reading.identification: Late-19th/early-20th-century four-storey brick corner block at Pensmarkt/Hooiaard in Ghent's medieval core, retail at ground level with dwellings above, on an amalgamated 13.6 m frontage under a long street-parallel gabled roof with an inhabited attic.
reading.notes:
EVIDENCE SPLIT. Only the roof is marked seen. Set A resolves one crisp orange ridge cap running the full length of the block with a single broad plane facing the square and a gable end at the right-hand party wall: gabled, ridge parallel to street, confirmed by both the plate and OSM roof:shape. Everything on the wall is typological inference for this street and period.

BAY RHYTHM: measured, count inferred. Column-luminance autocorrelation over the upper-floor band (y 450-590) gives a single dominant peak at lag 58 px, r=0.70 — a real regular fenestration rhythm, not tile noise. Converting it to a count requires a horizontal scale I cannot pin down, because this is a corner building (street_frontages=2) and I cannot locate the return corner well enough to say how much of the ~420 px visible face is the 13.6 m Pensmarkt frontage versus the Hooiaard return. At ~25 px/m the 58 px period is ~2.3 m centres, giving 6 bays; that also sits mid-band for an amalgamated 13.6 m Ghent retail frontage. 5 bays at ~2.7 m centres is the live alternative — if the generator can tolerate it, 6 is the better default but this is the least-secure number in the set. Naive per-row minima detection returned 12-19 spurious peaks; ignore that, the autocorrelation is the trustworthy statistic.

HEIGHT BUDGET closes against the confirmed 16.0 m: 3.8 ground + 3 x 2.9 upper = 12.5 m eaves, leaving 3.5 m ridge rise over the 4.7 m half-span (footprint depth 9.4 m) for a ~37 deg pitch. That matches the moderate, non-steep slope in the plate. It also leaves a habitable attic, which is consistent with two pale rectangles resolvable on the front pitch — roof lights or small dormers. They are at the very edge of resolution and I cannot separate flush rooflight from dormer, so I have not claimed them; if the generator places roof openings on the front pitch, that is defensible, but do not mark them seen.

DO NOT INHERIT THE GRASLEI PRIOR. This is one block behind Graslei, and the reflex answer for that quarter is a stepped or spout gable turned end-on to the water. The plate contradicts it: eaves-to-street, ridge-along-street, unbroken across a 13.6 m plot. That plot width is itself the tell — it is two or three medieval plots merged, so the surviving-guild-house grammar (narrow, vertical, gable-fronted, deep stone reveals) is the wrong template here. I have set reveal_class to shallow (~0.12 m) accordingly: shallow is what a 19th-century brick wall with segmental arches gives. Deep reveals belong to thick medieval or stone walls and would put too much geometry into the facade.

TRIM MATERIAL: the real material is blue Belgian limestone (arduin), the Ghent default for sills, lintels and shopfront surrounds. The enum has no limestone, so I selected marble — both are calcium carbonate with eps' ~7 and similar loss, which is the correct dielectric behaviour at 28 GHz. Concrete would have been the wrong permittivity for the right-sounding reason. Please do not "correct" this to concrete downstream.

PHYSICS PARTITION. Above 10 cm, ask for explicit geometry: window reveals, the stone sills, the floor-level string courses, the eaves cornice, and the shopfront fascia and stallriser. Those wedges are what set street-level field in this narrow square. Between 1 and 10 cm — brick relief and recessed mortar joints — is the roughness_mm 4.0 figure and a diffuse scattering coefficient, never mesh. Ghent historic brick with raked joints sits at 3-5 mm RMS; I have taken 4.0. Below 1 cm is permittivity only.

CLUTTER CALIBRATION — read the tags. fronting_street is highway=pedestrian with car_access=none, distance 0.0 m. Place NO vehicles at this facade. Pensmarkt adjoins the Groentenmarkt and is a market and terrace square; the plate shows exactly that clutter class in the open paved area to the right of the building — market stalls or parasols, street trees, and people. That, plus terrace furniture, A-boards, bins and bike parking, is the correct population. A generic park-cars-along-every-street rule would fill this square wrongly.

DETAIL BUDGET. The building has two frontages, both public and both close to the corridor, so concentrate resolution on the ground-floor shopfront line and the window heads and sills of the first floor, and on the eaves and gable silhouette which is the only edge this plate actually verifies. The rear and the party walls carry attached neighbours on both sides and deserve almost nothing.

CONFIDENCE 0.5: macro layer is solid — height confirmed, levels, brick and gabled roof from OSM, roof orientation genuinely seen. The entire opening grammar is a defensible instance rather than a recovered truth, and no street photograph exists to close the gap.
